## Reduction to $\mathbb{Z}_{15}$

Via the bijection $\phi:\{1,\dots,15\}\to\mathbb{Z}_{15}$, $\phi(i)=i\bmod 15$, setting $g=\phi\circ f\circ\phi^{-1}$ transforms the condition to:
$$g(g(x))=2g(x)-x \quad\text{in }\mathbb{Z}_{15}\text{ for all }x.$$
This is a bijection, so we count such $g:\mathbb{Z}_{15}\to\mathbb{Z}_{15}$.

## Structure of solutions

Let $T(x)=g(x)-x$. Then $g(x)=x+T(x)$, and the condition becomes:
$$g(g(x))=x+T(x)+T(g(x))=x+2T(x)\implies T(g(x))=T(x).$$

So **$T$ is constant on each $g$-orbit**. On an orbit where $T\equiv c$, we have $g(x)=x+c$, so the orbit is the coset $x+\langle c\rangle$, and $g$ acts as translation by $c$ — a single cycle. The functional graph has **only cycles, no trees**.

Conversely, any partition of $\mathbb{Z}_{15}$ into cosets of subgroups, with $g$ acting as translation by a generator of each subgroup, satisfies the condition. So we count such configurations.

## CRT decomposition

By $\mathbb{Z}_{15}\cong\mathbb{Z}_3\times\mathbb{Z}_5$, subgroups are $H_3\times H_5$ where $H_3\leq\mathbb{Z}_3$, $H_5\leq\mathbb{Z}_5$:

| Subgroup | Coset type | Size | # generators ($\varphi$) |
|---|---|---|---|
| $\{0\}\times\{0\}$ | single point | 1 | 1 |
| $\mathbb{Z}_3\times\{0\}$ | row (fixed $b$) | 3 | 2 |
| $\{0\}\times\mathbb{Z}_5$ | column (fixed $a$) | 5 | 4 |
| $\mathbb{Z}_3\times\mathbb{Z}_5$ | whole space | 15 | 8 |

## Counting valid partitions

**Key constraint:** A row $\mathbb{Z}_3\times\{b\}$ and a column $\{a\}\times\mathbb{Z}_5$ always intersect at $(a,b)$, so we **cannot mix rows and columns** in a partition. After choosing some rows, remaining elements can only form rows or points (columns would span covered rows). Similarly for columns.

**Case 1: Whole space as one orbit.** Choose a generator of $\mathbb{Z}_3\times\mathbb{Z}_5$: $\varphi(15)=8$ ways.

**Case 2: Rows + points (no columns).** For each of the 5 rows (indexed by $b\in\mathbb{Z}_5$), independently choose: make it a row orbit (2 generator choices) or split into 3 point-orbits (1 way). This gives $\prod_{b=0}^{4}(2+1)=3^5=243$ configurations.

**Case 3: Columns + points (no rows).** For each of the 3 columns (indexed by $a\in\mathbb{Z}_3$), independently choose: make it a column orbit (4 choices) or split into 5 point-orbits (1 way). This gives $\prod_{a=0}^{2}(4+1)=5^3=125$ configurations.

**Overlap:** Cases 2 and 3 share the "all points" configuration (1 way), where every element is a fixed point ($g=\mathrm{id}$). Case 1 is disjoint from both.

## Final count

$$\text{Total}=8+243+125-1=\boxed{375}$$
